painPoints.text: Scope creep — clients keep adding work after project starts
signals: "The deadline moves up but the scope doesn't shrink" — @oks_ios
"Everything got parked" — @philliplanos (scope creep after every meeting)
painPoints.exactLanguage: how do I get clients to stop adding work without losing the sale
painPoints.commercialIntent: Actively seeking solutions. Willing to pay.

painPoints.text: No single source of truth — clients don't know what's approved, what's in progress
signals: "The chaotic projects always start with a chaotic kickoff" — @HudecErik
"Feedback comes from 7 different people with 7 different opinions" — @oks_ios
painPoints.exactLanguage: where do I even send client updates so they stop asking me everything twice

painPoints.text: Client communication overhead — chasing clients for feedback, assets, approvals
signals: "No one can explain why the product exists" — @oks_ios
painPoints.exactLanguage: why can't clients just do what they're supposed to do so I can do my job
painPoints.commercialIntent: "I'll pay whatever it takes" tier. High urgency.

painPoints.text: Revision spirals — no clear revision limit or feedback process defined upfront
painPoints.exactLanguage: how many revisions is normal anyway
painPoints.commercialIntent: Annoying but not yet costing them significant money.

painPoints.text: No repeatable client workflow — every project is chaos, nothing systematized
signals: "Write everything down, map out your timeline" — @beyond_broke
"One source of truth" mentioned across 3 separate posts as the fix
painPoints.exactLanguage: is there a system for managing client projects that doesn't require a project manager
painPoints.commercialIntent: Building systems. Willing to invest in the right tool.
